title: 35% winners can beat 60% winners
hook: 60% winners vs 35% winners. Guess who's losing.
takeaway: How often you win is only half the math. A 60% win rate with small wins and big losses loses money; a 35% win rate with small losses and big wins makes it. The price of the second one is long losing streaks, so plan for them.
question: Can a 35% win rate beat a 60% win rate?
emotion: disbelief, then relief: the 'wait, what?' of a 60% winner losing money, then the relief that being wrong a lot is fine when the losses stay small

captions: 60% winners vs 35% winners. Guess who's losing.

props.title: Assumptions · simulated
items: Simulated: 1,000 runs of 100 trades each, seed 7
Mostly Right: wins 60%. +$100 a win, −$200 a loss
Mostly Wrong: wins 35%. +$300 a win, −$100 a loss
$10,000 account. Fixed dollar risk, no compounding
Every trade independent. No costs, slippage or gaps

captions: Same coin flips. Only the rules differ.
Right loses $20 a trade. Wrong makes $40.
How often you win is half of it.
Mostly Wrong's usual worst streak: 9 losses.
In a row. Feels awful. Plan for it.
